inputs.original_text: Five months after the ceasefire was announced, people in Gaza are still facing airstrikes, gunfire and shelling, and fishermen are still coming under fire at sea. That is not meaningful peace: civilians remain exposed to violence, while displacement has taken away homes and the livelihoods people need to survive. The language of “normality” cannot cover up who is bearing the cost. Protecting people and enabling them to rebuild must come before political claims of progress—and those with power must be held accountable for making that protection real.
inputs.modified_text: Five months after the ceasefire was announced, people in Gaza are still facing airstrikes, gunfire and shelling, including fishermen at sea. Calling this “normality” or progress means little when civilians remain exposed to violence and displacement has stripped people of homes and ways to make a living. The burden is falling on those with the least power, while those able to protect them must be held accountable. People’s safety and the chance to rebuild should come before political claims of success.
